item.title: 14 killed as truck carrying passengers, cattle crashes in Niger
item.description: NO fewer than 14 persons reportedly lost their lives in a road accident involving a DAF truck conveying 35 cattle and several passengers along Kontagora Road in Niger State. Zagazola Makama, a counter-insurgency publication, reported that the accident occurred around 11 a.m. on November 17 near Ibeto, as the truck, with registration number Lagos AZL 267 XH, travelled from Koko Local Government Area of Kebbi State to Lagos. “Police sources said an unidentified vehicle travelling in the same direction reportedly attempted to overtake the truck but brushed against it, causing the driver to lose control before the vehicle fell,” Makama said. “The truck driver and 13 other occupants reportedly died at the scene. “Those identified among the deceased included Umar, 45, the driver, from Kaoje; Anas Suleiman, 25, and Sufiyanu Suleiman, 40, both from Koko; Salim Abu Dogo, 30; Abubakar Shehu, 45; Yahaya Abubakar, 30; and Manu, 35, all from Dankigari. “Others were Rufai Umar, 25, from Bagudo; Faruk Tudu Kaoje, 20, from Kaoje; Umar Abubakar, 30, from Saradosa; Salisu Idry, 35, from Bagodo; and Abubakar Alhaji, 25, from Kaoje.” Police sources told Makama that relatives identified the bodies, while those claimed by their families were released for burial in accordance with Islamic rites. The publication added that two unidentified bodies had been deposited at the mortuary of Kontagora General Hospital. “The vehicle allegedly involved in the overtaking manoeuvre was later traced to Kaboji in Magama Local Government Area and taken to the Area Command Office,” Makama said. “However, the driver of the vehicle reportedly fled and remains at large.” According to the publication, the Niger State Police Command said investigation was ongoing to establish the full circumstances of the accident and apprehend the fleeing driver. The post 14 killed as truck carrying passengers, cattle crashes in Niger appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG issues Executive Order to end open defecation by 2030
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — The Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s efforts to eliminate open defecation by 2030, with state and local governments urged to strengthen sanitation financing, accountability and community mobilisation. The Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025, was unveiled on Thursday during the commemoration of World Toilet Day and the seventh anniversary of the Clean Nigeria campaign in Abuja. Vice President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Delivery and Coordination in the Office of the Vice President, Akubo Adegbe, described the Executive Order as a decisive step towards translating government commitments into measurable sanitation outcomes. Shettima said the order marked a transition from fragmented interventions to stronger coordination, measurable results and sustainable national progress. He disclosed that since the launch of the Clean Nigeria campaign in 2019, 185 of the country’s 774 local government areas had attained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, while Jigawa and Katsina remained the only states certified as open defecation-free. While acknowledging the progress recorded, the Vice President said Nigeria still had considerable ground to cover, urging states yet to achieve ODF status to establish monthly and quarterly targets and make their progress publicly available. He also warned against a reversal of gains in communities already certified as open defecation-free, stressing the need for sustained monitoring and accountability to protect existing achievements. According to him, achieving the 2030 target would require sustainable financing, reliable data, stronger institutions, effective implementation and continuous behavioural change. Shettima called on state and local governments to take ownership of the campaign by allocating adequate resources and strengthening sanitation institutions. He also urged development partners, the private sector, traditional rulers, community leaders and civil society organisations to sustain their support for the initiative. The Vice President, who chairs the Steering Committee of the Clean Nigeria Project, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to working with subnational governments, adding that the National Economic Council would also be deployed to advance and sustain the national sanitation agenda. Linking the campaign to this year’s World Toilet Day theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality”, Shettima highlighted the disproportionate burden poor sanitation places on women and girls. He said inadequate access to safe and private sanitation facilities undermined their health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. He therefore called for inclusive policies and investments that address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. item.title: Shettima, Issoufou reflect on Buhari’s legacy at biography launch
item.description: ‎–Late ex-President demonstrated leadership defined by character, not power –VP ‎–As Issoufou urges balanced assessment of Buhari’s achievements, controversies ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima and former President of Niger Republic, Mahamadou Issoufou, yesterday reflected on the legacy of the late former Nigerian leader, Muhammadu Buhari, describing his life and political career as an important chapter in Nigeria’s history that offers enduring lessons on leadership, character and public accountability. ‎ While Shettima said Buhari demonstrated that the true measure of leadership lies in personal character rather than the power and privileges of public office, Issoufou urged Nigerians to assess the former President’s legacy objectively, taking into account his achievements, decisions and controversies. ‎ ‎The two leaders spoke at the public presentation of “Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography”, a three-volume account of the former President’s life and political career, held at the Nigerian Army Conference Centre and Suites, Abuja. ‎ ‎The Vice President, who was represented by the Special Adviser to the President on General Duties, Office of the Vice President, Dr Aliyu Modibbo, said Buhari’s modest lifestyle, personal discipline and devotion to national service distinguished him from many political leaders. ‎ ‎Speaking on the theme, “The Life We Leave to History”, the Vice President recalled lessons from his personal relationship with the late President, particularly his indifference to material possessions and commitment to Nigeria. ‎ ‎”He taught me that the dignity of office depends upon the character of its occupant. He also taught me that a leader’s example continues to speak long after he is out of service,” Shettima said. ‎ ‎He described Buhari’s Spartan lifestyle as remarkable in a political environment where public office is sometimes pursued to satisfy private interests. ‎ ‎”His Spartan lifestyle distinguished him in a world where too many seek public office to satisfy private appetites. item.title: 2027: Inuwa leads APC campaign train through Kaltungo West
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe KALTUNGO — Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has led the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign train through the four wards in Kaltungo West constituency, with party leaders expressing confidence in the party’s victory in the 2027 general elections. Thousands of party supporters, faithful and residents turned out to welcome the governor and other APC chieftains during the campaign rallies, which covered Kaltungo East, Kaltungo West, Toungo and Ture wards. The rallies attracted large crowds of men, women and youths, with social and commercial activities temporarily disrupted as residents gathered to receive the campaign train. The campaign provided an opportunity for APC candidates and leaders to highlight the achievements of the Inuwa Yahaya administration, showcase ongoing development projects and solicit support ahead of the 2027 elections. Addressing supporters, Yahaya said his administration had demonstrated its commitment to improving the living conditions of residents through development projects across Kaltungo Local Government Area and other parts of the state. He said the APC-led administration remained committed to people-oriented governance, infrastructure development and the provision of essential services. The governor urged residents, particularly youths, to mobilise for the elections and vote for President Bola Tinubu and all APC candidates, stressing the need for continuity and consolidation of achievements at the federal and state levels. The APC governorship candidate, Dr Jamil Isyaku Gwamna, described Kaltungo as a strategic constituency in the political development of Gombe State. He urged residents to sustain their confidence in the APC and support its candidates before, during and after the elections. Similarly, the APC senatorial candidate for Gombe South, Hon. Jerry Joseph Damara, said the administrations of Tinubu and Yahaya had initiated and executed projects with significant impacts across the senatorial district. Damara appealed to the electorate to reciprocate the efforts of both administrations by voting for the APC, arguing that continued support would create opportunities for more development interventions. The APC candidate for Kaltungo/Shongom Federal Constituency, Hon. Binta Bello, commended Yahaya for facilitating the establishment of federal institutions in Kaltungo and implementing projects aimed at improving the socio-economic well-being of residents. She urged the electorate to support all APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Also speaking, the APC candidate for Kaltungo East State Constituency, Gabriel Galadima, described Yahaya as a worthy ambassador of Kaltungo, saying the administration’s development interventions demonstrated its commitment to the area’s growth. item.title: 2027: People Are Rejecting Tinubu, They Can Feel The Pain — Dele Momodu
item.description: A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, says Nigerians are rejecting President Bola Tinubu because they are feeling the adverse impact of his administration’s economic policies. Momodu, who is the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC presidential campaign council, said the growing public discontent was a reflection of the hardship Nigerians have endured since the removal of the fuel subsidy. The former Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential aspirant made the remarks on Thursday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today. A combo of Dele Momodu and President Bola Tinubu Momodu said the government should have carefully considered the advantages and disadvantages of the policy before implementing it. He likened the country’s economic situation to a patient who had been given an injection and remained in a coma for almost four years. “That’s what is happening in Nigeria. And that is why you can see that everywhere Tinubu goes now, he is being rejected by the people. The people are not stupid; they are rejecting him because they can feel the pain,” he said. ﻿ The publisher accused the President of insensitivity to Nigerians’ economic hardship, citing excessive government spending, inadequate funding of critical sectors and the burden of subsidy removal. “We’ve since discovered that this subsidy issue could have been better handled because, if you look at it, the people who are at fault are probably less than 1,000 people, and now you are punishing over 200 million Nigerians because of the sins of a few people. “If he were sharing in the pain of the people, he would not be doing what he is doing, donating one billion, doing a budget to individuals, a budget in trillions, more than what you are paying the military, more than what you are using to service the health sector, more than what you are spending on the education of our children,” Momodu said. Momodu accused the Tinubu administration of covertly reinstating fuel subsidies and dismissed positive economic assessments by the World Bank and IMF, arguing that they had not improved Nigerians’ living conditions. “The world is praising us; the World Bank is praising us; the IMF is saying we are doing well. Whenever the IMF or World Bank is interested in your case, then something is wrong. You can see clearly that everything you can say is not affecting our people positively. Nigerians are suffering, and that’s just the truth,” he said. Subsidy Removal, ‘Bamayi’ ﻿ Tinubu announced the removal of the fuel subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, citing its growing cost to government finances. Since that announcement, the policy, alongside the unification of the foreign exchange market, has contributed to higher petrol prices and increased living costs for Nigerians. item.title: Yiaga Africa Urges INEC To Publish Guidelines For Nov. 28 Mock Accreditation
item.description: Yiaga Africa has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish comprehensive guidelines and the list of participating polling units for its nationwide mock accreditation and electronic results upload exercise scheduled for November 28. The organisation said timely access to information about the exercise was necessary to enable citizens, political parties, civil society organisations, election observers, and the media to understand, participate in, and monitor the process. In a statement signed by its Executive Director, Samson Itodo, Yiaga Africa welcomed INEC’s decision to conduct the exercise ahead of the 2027 general elections. It said the exercise was consistent with sustained calls by citizens and civil society organisations for the commission to adequately test the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) before the elections. COMBO: Photo of YIAGA Africa executive director Samson Itodo and INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan “However, Yiaga Africa is concerned that, despite the importance of the exercise, the Commission is yet to make public comprehensive guidelines and a framework outlining how it will be conducted. The list of polling units where the exercise will take place is also yet to be made public. “For an exercise of this significance, timely access to information is essential. Citizens and electoral stakeholders should have sufficient information and notice to understand, participate in, and observe the process,” the statement read in part. Yiaga Africa said transparency in the exercise would be crucial to building public confidence in the electoral technologies that would be deployed for the 2027 elections. It called on INEC to immediately publish a comprehensive framework outlining the scope, modalities and procedures for the exercise. The organisation also urged the commission to release the complete list of participating polling units and other relevant locations early enough to give stakeholders sufficient time to prepare for the exercise. Yiaga Africa further urged INEC to use the mock exercise as an opportunity to demonstrate transparency and responsiveness while allowing meaningful public scrutiny of BVAS and IReV. Last week, INEC had announced November 28 as the date for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise to test its voter accreditation and electronic results transmission systems ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission’s chairman, Joash Amupitan, said the exercise would simulate the presidential election and take place across all states of the federation. He said the exercise was part of measures to address technical challenges experienced during the 2023 general elections and strengthen the credibility of the 2027 polls. The 2027 Presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will be held on February 6. item.title: When Ndigbo Become President, It Must Be Eight Full Years — Oshiomhole
item.description: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the South-East should have a full eight-year presidential tenure when a candidate from the region eventually becomes Nigeria’s president. The former Edo State governor spoke on Thursday at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State, where he endorsed President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. “When Ndigbo will become president, it must be eight full years. No half-talk. It will be full talk by those with brains, with courage, and fill the gap,” he said. Oshiomhole also praised Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo, a former governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), for his economic expertise and leadership. ﻿ He said Soludo understood the challenges facing Nigeria’s economy, particularly the disconnect between monetary and fiscal policies. Earlier, Soludo declared that President Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure victory, arguing that the President’s performance will earn him another term. “The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu and Shettima, they are doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” the governor said. Senator Oshiomhole’s comments on an eight-year presidential tenure for an eventual Igbo president come amid discussions about political power rotation and the South-East’s quest for the presidency. Igbo Presidency, Obi’s Stance Peter Obi speaking at NDC Town Hall meeting in Lagos. Photo: Nosakhale Akhimien/ChannelsTV Former Anambra State governor Peter Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election, is seeking the nation’s top job again in 2027 under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate. Obi, a South-Easterner, finished third in the 2023 presidential election with 6,101,533 votes, and has pledged to serve only one four-year term if elected, promising to hand over power to the North in 2031. ﻿ He has argued that a single term would allow him to focus on governance without the distractions of seeking re-election. He maintains that 48 months is enough time to tackle insecurity, fix the economy, and stabilise the country. However, the pledge has drawn criticism from some South-East political leaders, who believe the region should not concede a full eight-year presidential tenure. item.title: Trump, Putin, Xi agree to nuclear risk talks
item.description: By Favour Ulebor US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping have agreed to hold talks on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons following a trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China. The agreement was contained in a joint declaration issued by the White House on Thursday after the meeting, during which the three leaders discussed the international situation and pledged to promote strategic stability and international security. The United States, Russia and China, which are permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, also committed to reforming the UN to enable it to respond more effectively to global challenges and strengthen its role in maintaining international peace and security. The three countries further indicated plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products, while reaffirming the importance of stable energy flows. The leaders also addressed issues relating to the immunity of state officials and the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court (ICC), warning against what they described as the abuse of jurisdiction by the court and similar bodies. Trump and Putin also expressed appreciation to China for hosting the trilateral summit. The joint declaration read in part: “The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. “As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, the United States, Russia, and China committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security. “The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows. “The three heads of state recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of state officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.” The post Trump, Putin, Xi agree to nuclear risk talks appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: APC chieftain rejects Baba-Ahmed’s 2027 election prediction
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA – A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Hon. Aminu Shehu Sharada, has faulted the National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Dr. Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, over his prediction that the ruling party could suffer significant losses in the 2027 general elections, particularly in northern Nigeria. Sharada, in a statement he personally signed on Thursday, insisted that President Bola Tinubu enjoys political support in the North and would secure votes from the region in the 2027 presidential election. He specifically rejected Baba-Ahmed’s projection that the APC would struggle to genuinely win even two or three states in northern Nigeria, describing the assessment as an underestimation of the political awareness, democratic maturity and independent judgment of voters in the region. Baba-Ahmed had, in an interview, said it would be a miracle if the APC genuinely won two or three states in the North, citing what he described as public dissatisfaction with the ruling party at different levels. “On the basis of the current disposition of the public towards APC at all levels, it will be a miracle if they genuinely win two or three states in the North,” he had said. He also predicted possible APC losses across the South-East, South-South, parts of the South-West and North-Central. However, Sharada argued that the political support enjoyed by Tinubu in northern Nigeria should not be dismissed on the basis of assumptions or projections by political commentators. Defending the Tinubu administration’s record, the APC chieftain highlighted its economic reforms, infrastructure projects and interventions in education, healthcare, agriculture, housing and transportation. He cited the removal of petrol subsidy, unification of the foreign exchange market and ongoing tax reforms as major policy decisions aimed at strengthening public finances and attracting investments. He acknowledged that the reforms had generated considerable debate because of their immediate effects on household expenses, transportation costs and the general cost of living, but maintained that the administration considered them necessary for long-term economic stability. On infrastructure, Sharada listed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway and Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Road among major projects being pursued by the Federal Government. He also highlighted investments in railway modernisation, port improvements and electricity transmission. In education, he pointed to the establishment of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying the initiative was designed to reduce financial barriers to higher education and improve access to tertiary education. He also cited the Renewed Hope housing programme, healthcare interventions under the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and the Presidential Compressed Natural Gas Initiative as part of the administration’s development agenda. item.title: Tinubu should grant interviews to Nigerian journalists, Akande says
item.description: A former spokesman for ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande, has urged President Bola Tinubu to grant interviews to Nigerian journalists, saying the local media should have the opportunity to hold the President accountable. Akande made the call on Thursday while reacting to the controversy surrounding Tinubu’s interview with American political strategist and lobbyist, Diana London. He said he had no objection to the President granting an interview to a foreign journalist but questioned why Nigerian journalists had not been given similar opportunities to ask him questions on issues of national importance. “I wish the President were also having interviews with Nigerian journalists. That’s my own main issue with this development. “It’s not a bad thing that the President has chosen to have this interview; my worry is that he’s leaving out the Nigerian press. Why has he not made himself available for Nigerians to interrogate him?” he said. On allegations that London received $4.5 million in connection with the engagement, Akande said the strategist had denied being paid as a lobbyist by the Federal Government for the interview. He, however, called for greater transparency from the government to clarify the circumstances surrounding the engagement. “As to the controversy whether this woman (Diana) was paid, the woman has denied that she was doing this as a paid lobbyist of the Federal Government. The ADC people are saying that there should be more clarity, there should be more transparency, yes. “Let the Federal Government also give us more facts that this is not a paid-for interview. The most important thing is that Nigerians should be given the opportunity to interview Mr President,” Akande said. The former presidential spokesman also recalled his experience in the Presidential Villa during the administration of ex-President Muhammadu Buhari, when Osinbajo served as Vice-President. He said he considered it inappropriate for journalists invited to interview the President or Vice-President to demand payment for the opportunity. “My own experience in the Villa, I wasn’t aware of any payment for an interview and I expressed this. When we were in the Villa, I considered it an insult to have an opportunity to interview the President and the Vice-President and be asking for money. The President of a country is the numero uno,” he said. The controversy followed reports alleging that London received $4.5 million in connection with a lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government. London, who heads London Global Strategies, has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government or anyone else in the country. She said she travelled to Nigeria to interview Tinubu for a documentary and to experience the country. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar also questioned whether the interview formed part of the reported $4.5 million lobbying arrangement. item.title: Court restrains Jimmy Odukoya from parading as Fountain of Life senior pastor
item.description: The Lagos State High Court has restrained Jimmy Odukoya from parading himself as the Senior Pastor and spiritual head of the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin according to TheCable, granted the order on Wednesday following a suit instituted by the incorporated trustees of the church. The trustees had sought a pre-emptive order of injunction restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and interfering with its activities, governance and other affairs. They argued that Odukoya had ceased to hold the position following the appointment of a successor by the late founder and Senior Pastor of the church, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya. In the suit, the trustees sought an order restraining Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting, meddling with or obstructing the activities and governance of the church pending compliance with the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Directions No. 2 of 2019 on pre-action protocol. Granting the application, Justice Adewunmi-Oshin ruled: “Leave is hereby granted to the Applicant to commence this action under the Pre-Action Protocol pursuant to Paragraph 4 of the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019.” The order followed the trustees’ application for judicial intervention in the leadership and administration of the church. item.title: 2027: Atiku demands scrutiny of INEC’s AI system for processing election results
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to open its proposed artificial intelligence system for processing election results to independent audit ahead of the 2027 general elections. Atiku wants the commission to disclose how the technology works, who developed it and what safeguards are in place to prevent valid polling unit results from being flagged, delayed or excluded during electronic processing. In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said he had petitioned the INEC Chairman on behalf of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and allied democratic stakeholders, demanding algorithmic transparency, independent scrutiny and clear rules for human oversight. The petition follows INEC’s announced integration of artificial intelligence and intelligent document processing into the process linking its Data Verification and Authentication System, DIVAS, with the INEC Result Viewing portal, IReV. Warning against placing public confidence in an opaque technology, Atiku said: “INEC cannot ask Nigerians to trust a system whose rules they are forbidden to see. If an algorithm can flag a polling unit result sheet, the public deserves to know what triggers that flag, who set the threshold, who can change it and what happens to the result afterward.” He demanded publication of the system’s technical and operational framework, including its training data sources, criteria for flagging discrepancies and the identities of its developers and third-party vendors. He also wants independent cybersecurity experts, political party technology representatives and civil society technologists to have access to the source code, training data and decision logs for a comprehensive audit before the nationwide mock accreditation scheduled for November 28, 2026. On the legal status of polling unit results, Atiku insisted that the physical Form EC8A, completed and signed at the polling unit, must remain the primary evidence of what transpired there, warning against allowing an algorithmic assessment to override it. “The polling unit result sheet, Form EC8A, records what happened where the people voted. INEC must publicly reaffirm the legal status of the physical form completed and signed at the polling unit, and explain how it will resolve any conflict between that document and an AI assessment. “A machine’s verdict cannot be allowed to quietly displace the evidence witnessed by voters and party agents,” he said. Atiku also demanded a transparent procedure for reviewing flagged result sheets, including the officials responsible for such reviews, documentation of decisions, notification of political parties and mechanisms for promptly challenging errors. He proposed real-time monitoring access for political parties through a dedicated dashboard or observer interface to enable them to identify unusual patterns of flagging, delays or blocked uploads

item.title: Anambra home to political icons like Zik, Ekwueme, Soludo – Shettima
item.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – Vice-President Kashim Shettima has described Anambra State as a home of accomplished political leaders, citing Nigeria’s first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe; former Vice-President, Dr. Alex Ekwueme; and the incumbent governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo. Shettima made the observation on Thursday at a joint mega rally organised by the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) under the banner of Progressives Working Together. The Vice-President, who represented President Bola Tinubu at the rally, said he was not surprised that Soludo had embraced what he described as the visionary politics of national unity associated with Azikiwe and Ekwueme. He commended the governor for what he described as his courage and political approach in the current political dispensation. Shettima also assured Nigerians, particularly residents of Anambra State, that Tinubu’s administration would reposition the country if given another term in 2027. In his remarks, Soludo said APGA and APC had unanimously endorsed Tinubu for a second term in office. As part of the alliance, the governor handed over the APGA flag to the APC, describing the move as a demonstration of the parties’ commitment to working together. Soludo further disclosed that elected APGA members in the state and National Assemblies would work with their APC counterparts in their respective legislative caucuses. He said the arrangement was aimed at promoting cooperation, national unity and the indivisibility of Nigeria. item.title: Tinubu doesn’t need to rig 2027 election, Soludo says
item.description: Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, expressing confidence that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would win the contest. Soludo made the declaration on Thursday while speaking at a presidential campaign rally at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, where he argued that the APC had a stronger nationwide political presence than its opponents. “This election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The president doesn’t need to rig any election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig any election,” he said. Explaining his position, the governor said the APC presidential ticket was facing opposition candidates whose political influence, according to him, was limited to certain parts of the country. “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shettima ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others. “If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic in your mind, this election is literally over,” Soludo said. He also attributed his confidence to the performance of the Tinubu administration, arguing that the President and Vice-President Kashim Shettima deserved another term based on their record in office. “President Tinubu, Shettima, they’re doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he said. The governor further argued that the APC had presented a stronger policy agenda than its opponents, claiming that no credible alternative had emerged ahead of the election. “And let me put it on record, in terms of the agenda that they are pursuing, no candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria. “And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative. The Tinubu-Shettima ticket presidency is on course,” he said. Soludo also defended the Federal Government’s handling of the economy and security, claiming that there was a consensus among people familiar with the economy, both locally and internationally, that the administration was moving in the right direction. He cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which provides financial support to eligible students, as one of the initiatives through which the administration was addressing the needs of Nigerians. item.title: Kwara South: APC candidate Adewoye confident of victory

item.title: Sanwo-Olu gives LASUED best graduate N5m, job
item.description: By Elizabeth Osayande Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has rewarded the overall best graduating student of the Lagos State University of Education (LASUED), Blessed Mercy Olawunmi, with N5 million and automatic employment. The award was announced on Thursday, November 19, during the institution’s maiden convocation ceremony held at its Oto/Ijanikin campus. Olawunmi, of the Department of Home Economics, College of Vocational and Entrepreneurship Education, emerged top of the pioneering graduating class of 2,486 students, including 84 first-class graduates, with a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 4.98. Sanwo-Olu also announced a cash reward of N2.5 million each for the best graduating students from the university’s seven colleges. Apart from the governor’s award, Olawunmi received N250,000 and a commemorative plaque from the university, while Oto-Awori Local Government presented her with N1 million. The council chairman, Kareem Azeez Abiodun, also announced a reward of N500,000 each for the other best graduating students from the colleges. Speaking at the ceremony, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Bidemi Bilkis Lafiaji-Okuneye, thanked Sanwo-Olu for assenting to the law establishing the university in 2022. She also commended the Governing Council, staff, students and other stakeholders for their contributions towards making the institution a source of pride. However, she appealed to the governor to intervene in four areas requiring urgent attention: construction of a podcast and photojournalism studio, reconstruction of the perimeter fence, reclamation of swampy land at the main campus and completion of the 750-seat auditoriums at the Epe and Ijanikin campuses. The Vice-Chancellor disclosed that more than 60 per cent of the main campus land was swampy, leaving the institution with limited space for expansion. She said the university currently occupied only the dry portions of the land and was becoming increasingly cramped, adding that reclamation would provide room for future development. She noted that a female hostel being constructed by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) was already located on the site. “Your Excellency, sir, these four appeals are strategic investments rather than isolated requests. A studio will enrich what we teach. Secure fencing will protect people who teach — our land. Reclaimed land will create room for all that we still hope to build. An auditorium will provide a gathering space in which scholarship, professional development, and public engagement can flourish,” she said. Lafiaji-Okuneye also appreciated the Governing Council for its guidance and oversight, the Ministry of Tertiary Education for facilitating the university’s requests to the governor, and staff for sustaining the institution through its transition. item.title: Fubara inspects beach road, woos investors to Rivers
item.description: By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has expressed satisfaction with the progress of work on the Ngo-Atlantic Oyorokoto Beach Road in Andoni Local Government Area, urging prospective investors to explore the area’s tourism potential. Fubara gave the assurance on Thursday during an inspection of the project, promising that the access road to the beach would be asphalted before December and ahead of the next Tourists Beach Party. Speaking with journalists after the inspection, the governor said he visited the project site to assess the level of work, recalling that his administration had created an official access road to the beach before the declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers State. He said the project experienced some delays during the period but that the state government had since resumed meeting its obligations to contractors to ensure the development of the area into a tourism destination. “We’ve been following up and meeting our own side of the obligation to ensure that one of the promises that we made to our people that day — that we want to make this place a tourist centre — comes to reality. And that is one of the main reasons we came here to see what is happening and the extent of the job that has been done,” he said. Fubara described the inspection as an opportunity to assess first-hand the progress made on the project. He said work on the beach access road was largely satisfactory, adding that the major outstanding task was the asphalting of the road, which he assured would be completed before December or ahead of the next Tourists Beach Party. The governor also disclosed that he inspected the other section of the road leading to the fishing ports, where he said only a culvert, measuring about 100 metres from the fishing centre, remained to be completed. Fubara said the level of work recorded was significantly better than what was previously on ground. He urged prospective investors to take advantage of the area’s tourism and commercial opportunities, assuring them that they had nothing to fear about investing in Rivers State. item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Grand Alliance APGA has presented its flag to President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate at the All Progressives Congress APC campaign rally in Awka, Anambra State. APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, announced the alliance at the rally held at Alex Ekwueme Square on Thursday. “The chairman of PDP is not here, but he is well in his spirit. The chairman of Accord is here. We are four in one. Four political parties supporting one candidate. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Yilwatda then invited Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, to present the APGA flag, with Vice President Kashim Shettima receiving it on Tinubu’s behalf. Soludo said the handover made the rally unlike any other. He said it was the first time APGA was presenting its flag to the Tinubu/Shettima ticket as its presidential candidate. He also reminded the crowd that Anambra was where the ticket did worst in 2023. According to him, it recorded 5,111 votes, or 0.8 per cent. “Ndi Anambra, are we going to do far better than 2023? We will not be there again,” he said. The governor said Ndigbo would lose from another round of political isolation. “Let us make this campaign a conversation, not an argument among ourselves. In a democracy, what leverage do we have other than our votes and having alliance with the rest of the country?There is work to be done, but you don’t change a winning team”, he said. Soludo said power would move to the North in 2031 and that the South should first complete its eight years. item.title: Africa Records 71.4bn Transactions, $1.8trn Instant Payments In 2025 — Report
item.description: Africa’s instant payment systems processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, nearly three times the volume recorded in 2021, according to a new report by the AfricaNenda Foundation, the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the World Bank Group. The fifth edition of the State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS) report, published on Thursday, highlighted the rapid expansion of digital payment infrastructure across the continent but warns that access alone has not translated into widespread everyday usage. According to the report, 89 per cent of African adults live in countries with access to an instant payment system. However, a survey of 1,403 digital payment users across 15 markets found that 55 per cent still use cash for about half of their transactions. It also found that more than half of respondents had experienced payment problems, including delays and transfers to the wrong recipients, while one in three affected users never reported such incidents, largely because they did not know how to do so. “Five years ago, our first report mapped 29 instant payment systems; today there are 39, and one in two African adults live in a country served by an inclusive instant payment system IIPS,” said Sabine F. Mensah, who is Deputy CEO of AfricaNenda Foundation and lead author of the report. “The question has changed. It is no longer whether Africans can pay instantly, but whether they trust the system enough to stop reaching for cash. Our research shows that trust is won in seconds, through a payment that goes through instantly, with preventive safeguards such as recipient name validation, and a payment confirmation message received in real time. It is kept by getting timely resolution and people’s money back when something goes wrong.” (L-R): Deputy CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Sabine Mensah; CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Robert Ochola; and Deputy CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Akinwale Goodluck, at the report launch on Thursday, November 19, 2026. 39 Instant Payment Systems The report identified 39 live instant payment systems across Africa, comprising 35 domestic systems in 29 countries and four regional systems. Overall, 43 African countries now have access to instant payment capabilities through domestic or regional platforms. Four domestic systems were introduced in the past year in Liberia, Burundi, Guinea and Mauritania, while a new regional system now serves the eight countries of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). Another 17 countries have instant payment system projects underway. Transaction volumes, according to the report, have grown by an average of 28 per cent annually since 2021, while the average transaction value has declined from $45 to $26, indicating increased use for smaller, everyday purchases. item.title: [VIDEO] Drama As Ngige Urges Residents To Vote For APC ‘From Top To Bottom’ At Anambra Presidential Rally
item.description: There was a mild drama at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State on Thursday when a former governor of the state, Chris Ngige, urged residents to vote for the APC in the 2027 presidential, National Assembly, and House of Assembly elections. The former Minister of Labour and Employment, who spoke in Igbo, said Anambra residents had one target. “We will vote for the APC from top to bottom,” Ngige said, prompting reactions from participants at the rally, including Governor Charles Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), who stood beside him on stage and told his predecessor that the rally is a joint one. The former governor, who said he was not surprised by the reactions, later told members of APGA to vote for candidates of their choice. “Okay, members of APGA — freedom of choice — when you get to the polling booth, vote for the better place,” he said. Ngige added that while people were free to choose between APGA and the APC, Anambra desires to be connected to the Federal Government at the centre and get it through the ruling party. Earlier, the former minister said he remains a member of the APC, claiming that he brought the party to the South-East. “I am still a member of the APC, bona fide member, because I brought APC to the South East — 2013/2014,” he said. “The only thing is that I told people I am on sabbatical, but even if I am on sabbatical, my governor cannot be doing something, and the Vice President is coming physically, and the governor has called me to say we are here, and I would say I won’t come. No.” Ngige said people should not be forced but persuaded to vote during the 2027 general election. He also said those stopping people from campaigning are not doing so in the name of the APC. “We don’t want that — destruction of vehicles, stoning of people. No! We don’t want that.
